newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-NORMAN TO PLAY IN AUSTRALIA FOR FREE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NORMAN TO PLAY IN AUSTRALIA FOR FREE.

text.p: World number one Greg Norman has
agreed to play in his native Australia for free in a bid to
avoid another wave of criticism over appearance money.
Norman, stung by controversy over appearance money on
previous visits home, said he would forego his reported
A$250,000 (US$197,000) tournament fee to play in three
successive Australian Opens, starting in 1997.
"I'm playing the next three Australian Opens for nothing
because I'm getting so much flak about it all," Norman said on
on Monday.
"It's a tough decision on my part but every year I go back
to Australia and find I'm banging my head against the wall,"
said Norman, the defending Australian Open champion.
Norman's relationship with the Australian media has soured
badly in recent years, with some critics saying he could do more
to support the local tour, where he began his professional
career.
He said his treatment while playing in Australia earlier
this year was more hurtful to him than his subsequent defeat to
England's Nick Faldo at the U.S. Masters.
"It was the biggest hurt because I am Australian and I was
playing in Australia," Norman said.
Norman, the defending champion, is scheduled to play in this
year's Australian Open at The Australian course in Sydney
between November 21 and 24.
Norman, who normally makes at least one playing trip to
Australia each year, will then host his own tournament, The Greg
Norman Classic, at Royal Melbourne the following week.
In February this year, Norman came under fire for demanding
a reported A$250,000 fee to play in the South Australian Open in
Adelaide as the principal drawcard in an otherwise weak field.
